Just now

--

Sometimes, the smartest decision isn’t clicking “Apply.” It’s knowing when not to click at all.
Last night, I was doing something most of us avoid until our inbox starts screaming for help — I was cleaning up my Gmail.
I was sorting the important emails from the ones that had overstayed their welcome when one message stopped me in my tracks.
It was from someone claiming to be a recruiter from a well-known company.
According to the email, they had found my details in their internal database and thought I would be interested in a remote opportunity.
Now, if you’ve been job hunting for a while, you’ll understand why my heart skipped a beat.
This wasn’t just another newsletter.
It wasn’t another rejection.
It looked like the kind of email people hope to receive.
So tell me why…
I wasn’t excited.
Instead, I became suspicious.
The email wasn’t sent from the company’s official domain, and there was a link attached asking me to submit an interest form.
Immediately, two versions of me started arguing.
The job seeker in me was saying,
“Ogechi, what if this is real? Don’t miss this opportunity.”
But the Virtual Assistant in me had a completely different opinion.
“Something doesn’t feel right.”
One thing my Virtual Assistant training taught me is that not every professional-looking email deserves your trust.
Scammers have become incredibly good at making fake emails look convincing.
They know exactly what job seekers want to see.
And they know that excitement can make people ignore details they would normally question.
So there I was…
Staring at the screen.
Reading the email for the third time.
Wondering whether I was about to miss a genuine opportunity…
Or avoid becoming someone else’s success story.
Guess what I did next.
I came straight to ChatGPT. 😂
Being an introvert, ChatGPT has honestly become my go-to buddy whenever I need to think something through.
I uploaded a screenshot of the email and asked for an objective analysis.
What I appreciated most was that it didn’t rush to conclusions.
It pointed out the green flags.
The red flags.
And the things that simply couldn’t be verified.
That gave me enough information to make my own decision.
Instead of clicking the link inside the email, I went directly to the company’s official careers page and submitted my application there.
The email had asked me to notify the sender once I had applied, so I replied and let them know I’d completed my application.
Problem solved.
If the email was genuine, then my application still reached the company.
If it wasn’t…
Well…
They didn’t get me. 😂
The Lesson I Didn’t Expect
Looking back, this wasn’t really about one email.
It reminded me why attention to detail matters.
As Virtual Assistants, people often think our job is simply managing calendars, replying to emails, or organising files.
Those things are part of the job.
But another part, one that isn’t talked about enough is protecting information, verifying requests, and spotting potential risks before they become problems.
Sometimes your greatest value isn’t how quickly you respond.
It’s knowing when to slow down.
One careful decision can prevent one very expensive mistake.
That lesson doesn’t only apply to Virtual Assistants.
It applies to anyone working remotely, freelancing, job hunting, or simply navigating the internet today.
Sometimes…
The safest click is the one you never make.
What About You?
Have you ever received an email that looked completely legitimate but something just didn’t sit right with you?
Did you trust your instincts?
Or did you click first and ask questions later?
I’d genuinely love to hear your story in the comments.
